messages:
ashok: Heads-up — backup telemetry alert: last 24h shows ~1.2k archived objects missing CMK tag after yesterday's RBAC sweep. Anyone else seeing this?
backup-bot: [automated] s3-scan found 1,245 objects without tag 'x-redwood-cmk' in prod-bucket-archive. Investigate? :rotating_light:
maria: Was there a role rename during the RBAC cleanup?
devon: We renamed uploader-prod -> uploader-archive at 03:17 UTC. That might affect the principal used for KMS grants.
ashok: (typo fixed) ashok: Confirming: the backup agent obtains an ephemeral KMS grant for encrypt; if the IAM role ARN changed the grant lookup fails and the agent falls back to SSE-S3.
sam: Got a sample error from one backup-agent instance:
```text
2026-03-21T03:20:11Z backup-agent ERROR KMS Encrypt Failed: AccessDeniedException
caused by principal arn:aws:iam::123456:role/uploader-archive
backup-agent: falling back to SSE-S3 for object write
```
maria: yikes. Is this only object-store or DB snapshots too?
ashok: Quick audit query shows both: approx 400 DB snapshot uploads had Encrypt AccessDenied and the ~1,245 S3 PutObject fallbacks. Query we ran:
```spl
index=aws:kms OR index=aws:s3 eventName=Encrypt OR eventName=PutObject | where key_id="arn:aws:kms:us-east-1:123456:key/abcd-ef01" | stats count by eventName, errorCode
```
devon: Immediate mitigations (short list):
- revert role rename if possible (fast)
- create explicit KMS grant for new role ARN (fast)
- mark affected objects/snapshots for re-encrypt/reupload (medium)
maria: KMS grant example (short-lived grant recommended):
```bash
aws kms create-grant \ 
  --key-id alias/redwood-backups \ 
  --grantee-principal arn:aws:iam::123456:role/uploader-archive \ 
  --operations Encrypt Decrypt \ 
  --name "temp-grant-uploader-archive"
```
sam: Note: granting now won't retroactively encrypt objects that already used SSE-S3. Those will need rewrite.
backup-bot: Created remediation ticket RED-ENC-452 and uploaded audit CSV with object keys and snapshot IDs.
devon: For re-encrypt we can do a streaming copy that reads and writes objects with SSE-KMS. Plan: lambda batch or fleet job with concurrency=50, verify checksums after rewrite. Canary first.
maria: Also add preflight checks to CI for KMS grant presence and an observability rule: alert when PutObject returns SSE-S3 header or when kms:Encrypt returns AccessDenied > threshold.
ashok: I'm kicking off a canary re-encrypt for tenant=internal now; script will process 10 objects and post results. Script snippet: 
```python
import boto3
s3 = boto3.client('s3')
for key in keys:
    obj = s3.get_object(Bucket='prod-bucket-archive', Key=key)
    s3.put_object(Bucket='prod-bucket-archive', Key=key, Body=obj['Body'].read(), ServerSideEncryption='aws:kms', SSEKMSKeyId='alias/redwood-backups')
```
maria: Tasks: devon -> create grant + document IAM playbook; ashok -> run canary and sample re-encrypt results; sam -> verify DB snapshot encryption and run restore test for one canary snapshot; i'll update runbook + alerts and own the post-mortem.
devon: I'll create the grant now and paste the grant-id. If we need rollback we can retire the grant.
ashok: ETA ~2h to confirm canary + initial re-encrypt job. Will post success/fail logs in this thread.
maria: thanks. tagging @oncall and ops for visibility. Let's keep remediation off the critical path for customer-facing restores until we confirm DB snapshot integrity. :white_check_mark:
